builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: InterQ-RL: Interaction-Aware Correction of Execution Mismatch in Quantized Agentic RL
summary: InterQ-RL replaces current-token rollout-learner ratio correction (as in prior quantized-RL methods) with a bounded correction applied over the full state-reaching action history, distributing correction strength across segments under a fixed displacement budget. It requires no additional model forward pass, so the cost is implementation complexity in the importance-ratio computation rather than added memory or latency; W8A8-KV8 rollout itself reduces generation and KV-cache cost during long multi-turn rollouts. It can fail if the reader is not doing multi-turn agent RL at all (the correction targets execution mismatch along interaction histories, irrelevant to single-turn or SFT pipelines), if bounded prefix correction mis-allocates strength on environments with very long or sparse action segments, or if the reader's small models and environments differ enough from ALFWorld/WebShop/ScienceWorld with 4B-30B backbones that the mismatch it fixes is negligible.
rationale: The reader has the GPU budget for quantized small-model training and would benefit if running agentic RL, but the gain is specific to multi-turn RL rollouts and must be validated on their own environment and backbone before adoption.
technique: Interaction-aware prefix correction for quantized agentic RL

claims.statement: InterQ-RL replaces current-token rollout-learner ratio correction (as in prior quantized-RL methods) with a bounded correction applied over the full state-reaching action history, distributing correction strength across segments under a fixed displacement budget. It requires no additional model forward pass, so the cost is implementation complexity in the importance-ratio computation rather than added memory or latency; W8A8-KV8 rollout itself reduces generation and KV-cache cost during long multi-turn rollouts. It can fail if the reader is not doing multi-turn agent RL at all (the correction targets execution mismatch along interaction histories, irrelevant to single-turn or SFT pipelines), if bounded prefix correction mis-allocates strength on environments with very long or sparse action segments, or if the reader's small models and environments differ enough from ALFWorld/WebShop/ScienceWorld with 4B-30B backbones that the mismatch it fixes is negligible.

With W8A8-KV8 rollouts, InterQ-RL matches BF16 training to within 0.7 points across four environment-backbone settings (and exceeds it in two), while avoiding the late performance regression of alignment-only quantized RL.
